rv.q: “American Idiot,” directed by Michael Mayer and performed with galvanizing intensity by a terrific cast, detonates a fierce aesthetic charge in this ho-hum Broadway season.
The point here isn’t story but style, and American Idiot delivers its predictable message (life, especially its US variety, can sometimes suck) in spectacular fashion.
"American Idiot" is a rousing, cannily assembled stage spectacle.
Telling its story largely through music and movement with only a smattering of dialogue, “Idiot” never manages to make us care about the fate of its thinly drawn characters.
By the time it ends, 90 minutes later, you may feel more numbed than stirred.
Not that you'll need much prodding to fall for this fundamentally affectionate, surprisingly uplifting show.
The headache you're getting may be one you want to keep as the show is irresistibly propelled by the suggestive power of youth.
As someone who appreciates superior talent in any form, it's quite awesome.

Even with Gallagher thrashing around at its center, American Idiot satisfies in spite of all that's working against it—including the passage of time (and a presidency) that's rendered much of its discontent obsolete.
Still, punk nihilism and showbiz spirit-fingers are uneasy bedfellows.
On purely musical and visual levels, “American Idiot” reaches some exhilarating heights.
Nonetheless, the words take second place to the stunning visuals and staging.
American Idiot is instead a long string of cliches... it's ultimately derivative, boring theatre.

cn.t: Critics find Green Day's high-energy spectacle visually stunning but dramatically thin, with minimal character development and story. While some praise its visceral power and theatricality, others dismiss it as an overlong music video that breaks no new ground.

vs.sum: The St. James Theatre offers good sightlines for most seats, though the lack of a solid rake can be an issue if someone tall sits in front of you. The sound quality is generally good, but the tight legroom can be uncomfortable for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic and grand interior, while facilities are average with standard amenities.

acc.note: No steps from sidewalk to Orchestra. No elevator. Mezzanine up 29 steps, Balcony up 76 steps.
